cases.n: Epstein — Palm Beach police investigation and 2006 state charge
cases.victims_note: Palm Beach police identified about 35 girls (some accounts say 36); FBI interviewed 34 minors
cases.who: Jeffrey Epstein (financier)
cases.cover: Police chief Michael Reiter said state prosecutors under State Attorney Barry Krischer grew dismissive about six months in; he asked Krischer to step aside. The July 2006 state grand jury returned only one felony solicitation-of-prostitution count. Reiter then referred the case to the FBI.
cases.d: In March 2005 a woman told Palm Beach police her 14-year-old stepdaughter had been paid to give Epstein a massage at his mansion. A 13-month police investigation identified about 35 girls. In July 2006 a state grand jury returned a single count of felony solicitation of prostitution and Epstein was arrested on 23 July 2006. Reiter later called the outcome 'the worst failure of the criminal justice system' in modern times.
cases.cite: NBC News interview with former Palm Beach police chief Michael Reiter, 2019; DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility report, Nov 2020 (via Wikipedia)

cases.n: Epstein — 2007 federal non-prosecution agreement and 2008 state plea
cases.victims_note: FBI 'Operation Leap Year' interviewed 34 minors; plea required restitution to about three dozen victims
cases.who: Jeffrey Epstein; US Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida (Alexander Acosta)
cases.cover: Lenient deal: the federal non-prosecution agreement (2007) dropped federal charges against Epstein and 'several suspected co-conspirators' in return for a state guilty plea; it was kept from victims. Epstein served 13 months of an 18-month term, much of it on daily work release. In Feb 2019 Judge Kenneth Marra ruled prosecutors violated the Crime Victims' Rights Act by not telling victims while urging them to 'have patience'. DOJ OPR (Nov 2020) found Acosta used 'poor judgment' but committed no professional misconduct; an 11-month gap in Acosta's incoming emails was noted.
cases.d: After the FBI opened a federal probe, US Attorney Alexander Acosta's office negotiated a non-prosecution agreement in 2007. On 30 June 2008 Epstein pleaded guilty in Palm Beach County to soliciting prostitution and soliciting a minor; he was sentenced to 18 months, registered as a sex offender and was released on 22 July 2009 after 13 months. A 2018 Miami Herald series (Julie K. Brown) identified 80 victims and reopened scrutiny. Acosta resigned as US Labor Secretary in July 2019.
cases.cite: CNBC on Judge Marra's ruling, 21 Feb 2019; CNBC on DOJ OPR report, 12 Nov 2020; Wikipedia 'Jeffrey Epstein' and 'Alexander Acosta'

cases.n: Epstein — 2019 federal sex-trafficking indictment and death in custody
cases.who: Jeffrey Epstein; Metropolitan Correctional Center (Bureau of Prisons)
cases.cover: DOJ Inspector General (June 2023) found negligence and misconduct by Bureau of Prisons staff: 13 employees showed misconduct, two were criminally charged, guards skipped required checks and falsified records, and Epstein was left without a cellmate after an apparent July 23 suicide attempt.
cases.d: Epstein was arrested at Teterboro Airport on 6 July 2019 and indicted in Manhattan for sex trafficking of minors in 2002–2005. Bail was denied on 18 July. He died in his cell on 10 August 2019; the medical examiner ruled suicide by hanging and the case was dismissed on 29 August 2019. The DOJ Inspector General's June 2023 report found no evidence contradicting suicide but documented staff failures that made it possible.
cases.cite: DOJ Office of the Inspector General report on BOP custody of Jeffrey Epstein, June 2023 (via NBC News); Wikipedia 'Jeffrey Epstein'

cases.n: Ghislaine Maxwell — convicted of sex trafficking of a minor
cases.place: Manhattan, New York (trial); offences in New York, Palm Beach, New Mexico, London
cases.victims_note: four women testified to abuse as teenagers in the 1990s and early 2000s, including girls as young as 14
cases.who: Ghislaine Maxwell
cases.cover: In July 2025 Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche interviewed Maxwell with limited immunity; on 1 Aug 2025 she was moved to the minimum-security Federal Prison Camp Bryan, Texas. A DOJ official recorded secretly said the transfer was against policy (DOJ said he had no role).
cases.d: Maxwell was arrested on 2 July 2020 in Bradford, New Hampshire. On 29 December 2021 a jury convicted her on five of six counts, including sex trafficking of a minor; she was acquitted of enticing a minor to travel. She was sentenced on 28 June 2022 to 20 years. The Second Circuit upheld the conviction on 17 Sept 2024 and the US Supreme Court declined her appeal on 6 Oct 2025; she had argued Epstein's 2007 non-prosecution agreement shielded co-conspirators. As of mid-2026 her lawyer said he would seek a pardon; Blanche said in May 2026 he would not recommend one.
cases.cite: PBS NewsHour/AP, 6 Oct 2025; Wikipedia 'Ghislaine Maxwell'

cases.n: Jean-Luc Brunel — Paris investigation into rape of minors (died before trial)
cases.who: Jean-Luc Brunel; MC2 Model Management (New York/Miami), Karin Models
cases.d: The Paris prosecutor opened an investigation on 23 Aug 2019 into rape and sexual assault of minors and criminal conspiracy linked to Epstein. Model agent Jean-Luc Brunel, whose MC2 agency was reportedly launched in 2005 with up to US$1 million from Epstein, was arrested at Charles de Gaulle airport on 16 Dec 2020 while about to fly to Dakar. He was charged in June 2021 with raping a 17-year-old in the 1990s and later with rape of minors and sexual harassment. He was found hanged in La Santé prison on 19 Feb 2022; a 2023 inquiry ruled suicide. He denied wrongdoing and was never tried.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Jean-Luc Brunel' (citing AFP, Le Monde, Paris prosecutor statements)

cases.n: US Virgin Islands government suits — Epstein estate and JPMorgan
cases.place: Little St. James, US Virgin Islands
cases.who: Epstein estate; JPMorgan Chase; Deutsche Bank
cases.cover: Banks were alleged to have facilitated and concealed the operation by keeping Epstein as a client. New York's financial regulator fined Deutsche Bank $150m in July 2020 for ignoring red flags on Epstein. UK regulators permanently banned former JPMorgan banker Jes Staley (upheld June 2025) for recklessly misleading them about his Epstein relationship.
cases.d: Epstein bought Little St. James through L.S.J. LLC in April 1998; FBI agents searched it in August 2019. The USVI Attorney General sued the estate, which agreed in late 2022 to a $105m settlement, the largest in the territory's history. On 27 Dec 2022 USVI sued JPMorgan, alleging it knowingly facilitated Epstein's sex trafficking; JPMorgan settled with victims for $290m (June 2023) and with USVI for $75m (Sept 2023). The settlements carried no criminal findings.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Denise George', 'Jes Staley', 'Deutsche Bank', 'Little Saint James' (citing Reuters, NYT)

cases.n: Zorro Ranch, New Mexico — state probe dropped in 2019, reopened 2026
cases.place: Near Stanley, Santa Fe County, New Mexico
cases.victims_note: New Mexico legislative truth commission estimate of at least 30 people abused by Epstein or associates in the state, from survivor accounts and released files; ages not stated
cases.who: Jeffrey Epstein; New Mexico law enforcement
cases.cover: The state AG's 2019 investigation was closed at the request of the US Attorney's Office (SDNY). The 2026 interim commission report found Epstein likely got 'preferential treatment' from New Mexico law enforcement, avoided sex-offender registration via a loophole, and used NDAs, secrecy protocols and a $7m-a-year payroll to keep activity out of view. The FBI never searched the ranch in 2019.
cases.d: Epstein bought the 7,600-acre ranch in 1993. New Mexico AG Raúl Torrez reopened a criminal investigation on 12 March 2026 citing previously sealed FBI files, and state officials searched the ranch in March 2026 with the new owners' cooperation. A four-member legislative truth commission created in the 2026 session released a 119-page interim report on 5 Aug 2026; a final report is due by end of 2026. Allegations that bodies were buried near the ranch, raised in the files, are unconfirmed.
cases.cite: Daily Montanan/Source NM, 12 Mar 2026; Albuquerque Journal, 5 Aug 2026; Wikipedia 'Zorro Ranch'

cases.n: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor — civil settlement, loss of titles, 2026 arrest (misconduct in public office)
cases.who: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor (formerly Prince Andrew, Duke of York)
cases.cover: Settled civil case with no admission of liability (Feb 2022). In Oct 2025 it was alleged he asked a protection officer to investigate his accuser; the Metropolitan Police took no further action.
cases.d: Virginia Giuffre's court filings from 2014 alleged Epstein trafficked her to Andrew as a minor; he denies it. She sued in New York in Aug 2021; the case settled in Feb 2022 without admission (reported as about £12m). In Oct–Nov 2025 King Charles removed his remaining titles, including 'prince' (letters patent, Nov 2025). On 19 Feb 2026 Thames Valley Police arrested him on suspicion of misconduct in public office over reports from the DOJ files that he sent confidential trade-envoy reports to Epstein in 2010; he was released under investigation the same day. No sexual-offence charge exists; he denies wrongdoing; the investigation is ongoing.
cases.cite: PBS/AP, 19 Feb 2026; Wikipedia 'Relationship of Prince Andrew and Jeffrey Epstein'

cases.n: Peter Mandelson — 2026 arrest on suspicion of misconduct in public office (Epstein files)
cases.who: Peter Mandelson (former UK ambassador to the US, former cabinet minister)
cases.d: Mandelson was dismissed as UK ambassador to the US in Sept 2025 after emails showed he kept up his friendship with Epstein after Epstein's 2008 conviction. After the January 2026 DOJ release suggested he passed sensitive government information to Epstein about 15 years earlier, he left the Labour Party and House of Lords and the Metropolitan Police arrested him on 23 Feb 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office. He faces no allegation of sexual misconduct; recorded here for the network's political reach, not as an abuse case.
cases.cite: AP via WPTV, 23 Feb 2026; Wikipedia 'Epstein files'

cases.n: Thorbjørn Jagland — charged with aggravated corruption over Epstein ties
cases.who: Thorbjørn Jagland (former Norwegian PM, Council of Europe Secretary General, Nobel Committee chair)
cases.d: After the 2026 DOJ releases, Økokrim investigated whether Jagland received gifts, travel or loans from Epstein while chairing the Nobel Committee and leading the Council of Europe. The Council of Europe waived his immunity on 11 Feb 2026 and he was charged with aggravated corruption on 12 Feb 2026; properties were searched. He denies wrongdoing. This is a corruption case, not an abuse charge; recorded for the network's political reach.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Thorbjørn Jagland' (citing NRK, CNN, Reuters)

cases.n: Ankara prosecutors' inquiry into alleged trafficking of girls from Turkey to Epstein
cases.who: Ankara Chief Public Prosecutor's Office (inquiry)
cases.d: On 23 Dec 2025 Ankara prosecutors reportedly opened an inquiry after opposition MP Turhan Çömez cited the DOJ files. The underlying document is a May 2009 civil complaint by 'Jane Doe No. 102' alleging 'upon information and belief' that Epstein brought minor girls from 'Turkey, the Czech Republic, Asia, and numerous other countries'. Prosecutors are reviewing the files; no findings or charges have been reported.
cases.cite: Bianet, citing DW Türkçe, Dec 2025

cases.n: Epstein Files Transparency Act and DOJ releases (2025–2026)
cases.who: US Department of Justice; FBI; House Oversight Committee
cases.cover: DOJ said it identified about 6 million potentially responsive pages but released about 3.5 million, withholding about 200,000 under privilege, abuse material and victim-identity grounds; critics in both parties said it broke the law. Faulty redactions exposed at least 43 victims' names (WSJ). The DOJ Inspector General opened a compliance review in April 2026.
cases.d: A July 2025 DOJ/FBI memo said there was no 'client list', no credible evidence of blackmail and no basis to investigate uncharged third parties, and affirmed suicide. Congress then passed the Act 427–1 (House) and by unanimous consent (Senate); it was signed 19 Nov 2025. DOJ released files on 19–23 Dec 2025, about 3 million more pages on 30 Jan 2026, and restored about 50,000 removed files on 5 Mar 2026. The releases documented Epstein's continued contact with prominent people after 2008 and led to police inquiries in the UK and Norway and resignations in several countries; they did not establish a client list or prove claims that Epstein 'lent out' girls to powerful men, which FBI notes said other victims did not corroborate. The House Oversight Committee separately obtained the estate's 50th-birthday album from 8 Sept 2025.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Epstein Files Transparency Act' and 'Epstein files' (citing NPR, CNN, DOJ statements); CBS News, 30 Jan 2026

cases.n: Claims that Epstein was tied to intelligence services
cases.who: Claims about US and Israeli intelligence (unproven)
cases.d: In July 2019 journalist Vicky Ward (Daily Beast) cited an anonymous former White House official saying Acosta told transition vetters he had been told Epstein 'belonged to intelligence' and to leave it alone. Acosta denied this, and DOJ's Office of Professional Responsibility (Nov 2020) found no evidence Epstein was a cooperating witness or intelligence asset. Former Israeli intelligence figure Ari Ben-Menashe has claimed Robert Maxwell (Ghislaine's father) was a Mossad agent; Congress's Iran-Contra investigators called his testimony 'not credible'. Documented: Epstein had a close business relationship with former Israeli PM Ehud Barak (investment in Reporty/Carbyne, about 30 visits 2013–2017); Barak denies wrongdoing. No official body has found that Epstein worked for any intelligence service.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Alexander Acosta' (citing Daily Beast, 9 Jul 2019, and OPR report Nov 2020); Wikipedia 'Ari Ben-Menashe'; Wikipedia 'Ehud Barak'

cases.n: Jimmy Savile — 'Giving Victims a Voice' (Met Police/NSPCC)
cases.victims_note: 589 alleged victims came forward to Operation Yewtree, 450 alleging abuse by Savile; 214 offences recorded as crimes, 34 of them rape or penetration
cases.who: Jimmy Savile (BBC broadcaster); BBC; NHS hospitals; Metropolitan Police
cases.cover: Earliest known police report dates from 1958, with police intelligence from 1963; Surrey Police investigated in 2007–09 without charges. A BBC Newsnight investigation was shelved in December 2011; the Pollard Review called the decision flawed.
cases.d: After Savile's death in October 2011, an ITV documentary on 3 Oct 2012 carried accounts of abuse of teenage girls. The Metropolitan Police opened Operation Yewtree on 19 Oct 2012. The January 2013 Met/NSPCC report 'Giving Victims a Voice' recorded 214 crimes, including 34 rape or penetration offences. The scandal was a major reason for creating the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (IICSA).
cases.cite: Metropolitan Police & NSPCC, 'Giving Victims a Voice', Jan 2013 (via Wikipedia 'Jimmy Savile sexual abuse scandal')

cases.n: Dame Janet Smith Review — Savile and Stuart Hall at the BBC
cases.victims_note: 72 people abused by Savile in connection with BBC work, 8 raped, youngest aged 8; separately at least 21 female victims of Stuart Hall at the BBC 1967–1991, youngest 10
cases.who: BBC
cases.cover: Some BBC staff knew of complaints about Savile and Hall but did not pass them to senior management; Hall's celebrity status discouraged staff from escalating.
cases.d: The independent review by Dame Janet Smith, published in February 2016, found that Savile sexually abused 72 people in connection with his BBC work, raping eight, the youngest aged eight. It found that Stuart Hall assaulted at least 21 girls and women at the BBC, the youngest aged 10. Some staff knew of complaints, but these were not escalated.
cases.cite: Dame Janet Smith Review, Feb 2016 (via Wikipedia 'Jimmy Savile sexual abuse scandal' and 'Stuart Hall (presenter)')

cases.n: Lampard report — Savile in NHS hospitals
cases.place: Leeds General Infirmary, Stoke Mandeville, Broadmoor and other NHS sites
cases.victims_note: 60 people said they were abused at Leeds General Infirmary; more than 50 at Stoke Mandeville; victims aged 5 to 75 across NHS sites
cases.who: NHS hospitals (Leeds General Infirmary, Stoke Mandeville, Broadmoor and others)
cases.d: Kate Lampard's investigation (reports June 2014 and February 2015) summarised 44 NHS investigations and found Savile abused patients, staff and visitors aged 5 to 75 in NHS hospitals, where his celebrity and fundraising gave him keys and access. At Leeds General Infirmary 60 people said they were abused.
cases.cite: Kate Lampard, 'Themes and lessons learnt from NHS investigations into matters relating to Jimmy Savile', Feb 2015 (via Wikipedia)

cases.n: Cyril Smith MP — Cambridge House and Knowl View, Rochdale
cases.victims_note: 144 complaints reported by April 2014, victims as young as eight
cases.who: Cyril Smith (Liberal MP for Rochdale 1972–1992); Lancashire Constabulary; Director of Public Prosecutions; Rochdale Council
cases.cover: Police evidence presented in 1970 led to no action; the CPS said in 2012 that Smith should have been charged and that he had been given an assurance in 1970 he would not be prosecuted. Press allegations in 1979 (Rochdale Alternative Press, Private Eye) produced no prosecution. He was knighted in 1988 though Margaret Thatcher had been told of the allegations.
cases.d: Cyril Smith was alleged to have sexually and physically abused teenage boys at the Cambridge House hostel he co-founded in Rochdale in the 1960s and at Knowl View school. He died in 2010, never charged. In November 2012 Greater Manchester Police cited 'overwhelming evidence' of abuse of young boys. The IICSA report on Cambridge House, Knowl View and Rochdale (April 2018) examined why he was never prosecuted; Rochdale Council removed his Freedom of the Borough in October 2018.
cases.cite: IICSA, 'Cambridge House, Knowl View and Rochdale' investigation report, April 2018; CPS statement Nov 2012 (via Wikipedia 'Cyril Smith')

cases.n: Elm Guest House, London — VIP-abuse claims
cases.who: Elm Guest House; Metropolitan Police (Operation Fernbridge)
cases.d: Police raided the guest house in 1982 and the owners were charged with running a disorderly house. Claims from 1990 onward that politicians visited were investigated in Operation Fernbridge (2013–2015); its prosecutions did not expose abuse linked to Elm. At IICSA in 2019 Commander Neil Jerome said that, apart from a child removed during the raid, no credible victim had alleged an offence there and no prominent person was conclusively identified. A 10-year-old boy removed in the raid had been raped, so abuse occurred; the VIP claims are unsupported.
cases.cite: IICSA Westminster hearings, Feb 2019 (via Wikipedia 'Elm Guest House')

cases.n: Operation Midland — Carl Beech's false 'VIP ring' claims
cases.who: Metropolitan Police; Carl Beech (complainant)
cases.d: Between November 2014 and March 2016 the Met investigated Carl Beech's claims that a VIP ring of politicians and generals abused boys and committed murders, including at Dolphin Square. It searched homes and named suspects, including Leon Brittan, Harvey Proctor and Lord Bramall, but charged no one. Sir Richard Henriques's review (Nov 2016) found the accused were victims of false allegations. In July 2019 Beech was convicted of perverting the course of justice and fraud and, separately, of child sexual offences including indecent images; he was jailed for 18 years.
cases.cite: Henriques review, Nov 2016; Newcastle Crown Court, July 2019 (via Wikipedia 'Operation Midland')

cases.n: IICSA Westminster report — deference and failures (no proven 'VIP ring')
cases.who: Parliament; political parties; police; Director of Public Prosecutions
cases.cover: Example of documented deference: in 1978 diplomat Peter Hayman left child-abuse-related material on a London bus; police found 45 diaries of sexual fantasies about children, but the DPP advised no prosecution; Attorney General Havers defended this in 1981 after MP Geoffrey Dickens named Hayman in the Commons.
cases.d: IICSA held an investigation into allegations of child sexual abuse linked to Westminster (report February 2020). Its findings are NOT summarised here because the report could not be opened in this pass; check before publishing. What is documented from opened sources: the Hayman case (no prosecution in 1978–81 despite seized material) and IICSA evidence on Elm Guest House (see that record).
cases.cite: IICSA, 'Allegations of child sexual abuse linked to Westminster', Feb 2020; Wikipedia 'Peter Hayman (diplomat)'

cases.n: Rolf Harris — convicted of indecent assault of girls
cases.who: Rolf Harris (entertainer)
cases.d: Arrested in March 2013 under Operation Yewtree, Harris was found guilty on 30 June 2014 of 12 counts of indecent assault against four girls and young women between the 1960s and 1986, one aged eight. He was sentenced to five years nine months. In 2017 the Court of Appeal quashed one conviction; the other 11 stood. He died in 2023.
cases.cite: Southwark Crown Court, 30 Jun & 4 Jul 2014 (via Wikipedia 'Rolf Harris')

cases.n: Gary Glitter (Paul Gadd) — UK, Cambodia and Vietnam cases
cases.victims_note: two girls aged 10 and 11 in Vietnam; three girls in UK 1975–1980
cases.who: Paul Gadd ('Gary Glitter', pop singer)
cases.d: Convicted in the UK in 1999 of possessing over 4,000 child abuse images (4 months). He was expelled from Cambodia in 2002–03. In 2006 a Vietnamese court convicted him of obscene acts with two girls aged 10 and 11 (3 years). In 2015, after Operation Yewtree, he was convicted of attempted rape and indecent assault of three girls in 1975–1980 and sentenced to 16 years; recalled to prison in March 2023.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Gary Glitter' (citing court reports)

cases.n: Stuart Hall — indecent assault of girls (BBC presenter)
cases.victims_note: 13 girls aged 9–17 in the 2013 plea; Smith review found at least 21 victims at the BBC
cases.who: Stuart Hall (BBC broadcaster)
cases.d: In April 2013 Hall pleaded guilty to 14 counts of indecent assault on 13 girls aged 9 to 17; his 15-month sentence was doubled to 30 months as unduly lenient. In May 2014 he was convicted of two more counts involving a 13-year-old (total five years).
cases.cite: Preston Crown Court 2013–14 (via Wikipedia 'Stuart Hall (presenter)')

cases.n: Max Clifford — indecent assault
cases.victims_note: four victims aged 15–19
cases.who: Max Clifford (publicist)
cases.d: Clifford was convicted in April 2014 of eight counts of indecent assault against four victims aged 15 to 19 and jailed for eight years; his appeal failed. He died in prison in December 2017.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Max Clifford'

cases.n: Operation Yewtree — post-Savile investigation of public figures
cases.who: Metropolitan Police
cases.d: Launched on 19 Oct 2012, Yewtree arrested 19 people by Oct 2015; seven were convicted (Gadd, Dave Lee Travis on one count, Clifford, Harris, Chris Denning, Michael Salmon, Geoffrey Wheeler). Others were acquitted or never charged, including several well-known names, and must not be described as offenders.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Operation Yewtree'

cases.n: Huw Edwards — indecent images of children
cases.who: Huw Edwards (BBC newsreader)
cases.cover: The BBC kept paying him after his November 2023 arrest; it later asked him to repay over £200,000.
cases.d: BBC newsreader Huw Edwards was arrested on 8 Nov 2023 and pleaded guilty on 31 July 2024 to three counts of making indecent images of children, received via WhatsApp (41 of 377 images sent by another man were indecent images of children). On 16 Sept 2024 he received six months suspended for two years.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Huw Edwards' (citing BBC, CPS)

cases.n: Barry Bennell and English youth football (Sheldon Review)
cases.victims_note: Operation Hydrant by July 2018: 849 alleged victims, about 300 suspects, 340 clubs (all of football, not Bennell alone); Bennell convicted for offences against at least 12 boys in 2018 plus earlier victims
cases.who: Barry Bennell (coach/scout, Crewe Alexandra, Manchester City links); The Football Association
cases.cover: Crewe Alexandra heard an allegation but kept Bennell on with restrictions (former director Hamilton Smith). The Sheldon Review found the FA guilty of 'institutional failure' for delaying safeguards after 1995.
cases.d: Bennell was convicted in Florida in 1994 (abuse of a 13-year-old club player), at Chester in 1998 (23 offences, six boys), in 2015, in Feb 2018 (50 offences against 12 boys; 31 years) and in 2020. After former player Andy Woodward spoke out in Nov 2016 more than 350 alleged victims came forward within a month. Clive Sheldon QC's review (17 Mar 2021) criticised the FA and eight clubs. By end-2021, 14 men had been convicted. Bennell died in prison in 2023.
cases.cite: Sheldon Independent Review, 17 Mar 2021; Wikipedia 'Barry Bennell'

cases.n: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry — elite boarding schools (Fettes, Loretto, Gordonstoun, Edinburgh Academy, Merchiston)
cases.who: Fettes College, Loretto School, Gordonstoun, Edinburgh Academy, Merchiston Castle School
cases.cover: Fettes dismissed teacher Iain Wares in 1979 but gave him a glowing testimonial; he went on to teach in South Africa.
cases.d: The Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry found or heard admissions of sexual abuse at elite independent schools: Fettes accepted Iain Wares molested junior boys in 1973–79; Loretto admitted abuse by a teacher in the 1950s–60s; at Gordonstoun 11 alleged abuse incidents included the rape of a 13-year-old girl by an instructor; Merchiston admitted abuse between 1930 and 2014. The inquiry estimated about three quarters of children in Wares's Edinburgh Academy classes were abused. South Africa approved Wares's extradition, which he was still fighting in 2025.
cases.cite: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry boarding-school case study findings, 2021–2023 (via Wikipedia 'Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry' and 'Edinburgh Academy')

cases.n: Dutroux affair — kidnap, abuse and murder of girls; police and justice failures
cases.victims_note: six girls kidnapped in 1995–96, four died; earlier 1989 conviction for five girls
cases.who: Marc Dutroux, Michelle Martin, Michel Lelièvre; Belgian Gendarmerie and judicial police
cases.cover: Dutroux was released early in 1992 from a 13.5-year sentence over prosecutor and psychiatrist objections. Police missed chances, including voices heard in his cellar and unreviewed videotapes; rivalry between Gendarmerie and judicial police hampered the hunt. Judge Connerotte was removed in Oct 1996 for attending a victims' fundraising dinner.
cases.d: Dutroux kidnapped six girls in 1995–96; four died. He was arrested on 13 Aug 1996; about 300,000 people joined the White March on 20 Oct 1996. The Verwilghen parliamentary commission (Feb 1998) found 'corruption, carelessness and incompetence' but no high-level protectors. On 22 June 2004 he was sentenced to life; Martin got 30 years and Lelièvre 25; businessman Michel Nihoul was acquitted of kidnapping and convicted on drug charges. Belgium reorganised its police forces.
cases.cite: Verwilghen parliamentary commission, Feb 1998; Arlon assize court, 22 Jun 2004 (via Wikipedia 'Marc Dutroux')

cases.n: Dutroux 'X-dossiers' — witness claims of an elite abuse network
cases.who: Witnesses X1–X4 (claims); Belgian prosecutors
cases.d: Witnesses including Régina Louf told investigators in 1996–97 of abuse parties and unsolved murders involving Dutroux and Nihoul and prominent people. Prosecutors ultimately dismissed her statements, and investigators were criticised for leading her; an officer charged in 1997 with falsifying her statements was cleared in 1999. The parliamentary commission found no high-level protectors. The claims remain unproven; a 1999 book by three journalists argued the witnesses were more credible than portrayed.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Marc Dutroux' (citing Verwilghen commission and press)

cases.n: Casa Pia — abuse of children in state care by a TV presenter, diplomat and others
cases.victims_note: 32 alleged victims testified at trial
cases.who: Casa Pia (state children's institution); Carlos Cruz (TV presenter); Jorge Ritto (ex-ambassador); Hugo Marçal (lawyer); Ferreira Diniz (doctor); Manuel Abrantes (Casa Pia official); Carlos Silvino (driver)
cases.cover: A teacher reportedly began reporting abuse to Casa Pia leaders and police in 1975, and police accused a caretaker in 1981, without legal action. Ritto had been removed as consul in Stuttgart around 1969–71 after a complaint about an under-age boy, but stayed in the diplomatic service.
cases.d: The scandal broke in Sept–Nov 2002 (Felícia Cabrita, Expresso). After a trial from 2004, on 3 Sept 2010 six men were convicted: driver Carlos Silvino (18 years), TV presenter Carlos Cruz (7), doctor Ferreira Diniz (7), ex-ambassador Jorge Ritto (6y8m), lawyer Hugo Marçal (6y2m) and Casa Pia official Manuel Abrantes (5y9m). Former minister Paulo Pedroso was detained but charges were dropped and he won €100,000 for wrongful detention.
cases.cite: Lisbon criminal court verdict, 3 Sept 2010 (via Wikipedia 'Casa Pia child sexual abuse scandal')

cases.n: Joris Demmink allegations (Netherlands) — investigated, never charged
cases.who: Allegations against the former Secretary-General of the Dutch Ministry of Justice
cases.d: In 2007 an imprisoned Turkish man alleged that Demmink raped two boys in Turkey in the late 1990s; a criminal complaint followed in 2010. An appeals court ordered an investigation in January 2014; in June 2016 prosecutors said it produced no reliable evidence, and it was discontinued in 2017 (no evidence he was in Turkey; Turkey did not cooperate). Demmink was never charged and denies the allegations.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Joris Demmink' (citing Dutch Public Prosecution Service, NOS)

cases.n: Gabriel Matzneff — writer's published accounts of abusing minors
cases.who: Gabriel Matzneff (author); French literary establishment (Gallimard and others)
cases.cover: Literary tolerance: Matzneff published diaries describing sex with minors and child sex tourism in the Philippines (e.g. 1985) and was celebrated on TV (Apostrophes, 1990).
cases.d: Vanessa Springora's 'Le Consentement' (late 2019/Jan 2020) described his relationship with her at 14. Gallimard withdrew his books in January 2020, and Paris prosecutors opened an investigation for rape of a minor under 15; police searched Gallimard on 12 Feb 2020. The case was dismissed because the statute of limitations had expired.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Gabriel Matzneff' (citing Le Monde, AFP)

cases.n: Olivier Duhamel — incest allegation ('La Familia grande')
cases.who: Olivier Duhamel (constitutional scholar, head of Sciences Po foundation FNSP)
cases.d: In January 2021 Camille Kouchner's book alleged that Duhamel abused her twin brother, his 13-year-old stepson, in 1988. Paris prosecutors opened an investigation on 5 Jan 2021; Duhamel resigned his posts. In April 2021 French media, citing sources close to the investigation, reported he admitted the abuse. The facts were time-barred.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Olivier Duhamel' (citing Le Monde, AFP)

cases.n: Joël Le Scouarnec — surgeon convicted for 299 victims
cases.victims_note: 256 under 15; youngest 1
cases.who: Joël Le Scouarnec (surgeon); hospitals and medical regulators
cases.cover: The FBI traced his downloading of abuse images in 2004; his 2005 conviction (4 months suspended) brought no restriction on practice. Prosecutors did not alert medical authorities; the regional medical body found no breach in 2006; a 2007 warning to the health ministry brought no action; a hospital hired him in 2008 knowing of the conviction.
cases.d: Le Scouarnec, a surgeon in western France, was convicted in Saintes in Dec 2020 of raping and assaulting four children (15 years). On 28 May 2025 the Vannes court convicted him of offences against 299 victims, mostly hospital patients under 15, between 1989 and 2014, and imposed the maximum 20 years. He is not part of an elite network; included as a professional whose standing protected him (setting is debatable — could be moved to 'care').
cases.cite: Vannes criminal court, 28 May 2025 (via Wikipedia 'Joël Le Scouarnec')

cases.n: Hungary — presidential pardon in Bicske children's-home cover-up case
cases.who: President Katalin Novák; Justice Minister Judit Varga; Bicske children's home
cases.cover: In April 2023 the president pardoned the home's former deputy director, Endre Kónya, who had been convicted of helping cover up the director's sexual abuse of children.
cases.d: The pardon became public on 2 Feb 2024. President Novák resigned on 10 Feb 2024 and Justice Minister Varga, who countersigned it, left politics the same day; Reformed Church leader Zoltán Balog resigned on 16 Feb. It is the only case in this set where a head of state resigned over a child-abuse cover-up pardon.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Katalin Novák' (citing 444.hu, Reuters)

cases.n: Lord Greville Janner — allegations from Leicestershire children's homes; never tried
cases.victims_note: CPS found evidence for 22 counts against nine alleged victims (1969–1988); police later had information from 25 alleged victims
cases.who: Greville Janner (Labour MP and peer); Leicestershire Police; Crown Prosecution Service
cases.cover: Police investigated in 1991, 2002 and 2007 without charges. The Henriques report (Jan 2016) found the CPS and police at fault and said a prosecution was likely to have succeeded in 1991, 2002 or 2007. A 2021 review found police 'appeared reluctant to fully investigate'.
cases.d: Allegations that Janner abused boys in Leicestershire children's homes were first made in 1991. In April 2015 the CPS decided not to charge him because of dementia; a review reversed this in June 2015, but he was found unfit to plead in Dec 2015 and died on 19 Dec 2015 before a 'trial of the facts'. He was never convicted; the official findings concern the failure of police and prosecutors to act.
cases.cite: Henriques report on CPS/police handling, Jan 2016 (via Wikipedia 'Greville Janner')

cases.n: Kincora Boys' Home, Belfast — abuse and intelligence-cover-up claims
cases.who: Kincora Boys' Home staff (William McGrath, Raymond Semple, Joseph Mains); RUC; claims about MI5
cases.cover: Allegations reached the RUC in 1977 and a report went to the DPP, but abuse continued until 1980. Claims that MI5 used McGrath as an informer and obstructed police (Martin Dillon; former officers Colin Wallace and Brian Gemmell) were examined by the HIA inquiry, which found no state or intelligence collusion but blamed poor police investigation; it could not compel security services to testify.
cases.d: Kincora was a state hostel for boys aged 15–18. Abuse became public on 24 Jan 1980 (Irish Independent); three staff were charged in April 1980 and convicted (Mains 6 years, Semple 5, McGrath 4). Sir Anthony Hart's Historical Institutional Abuse Inquiry (20 Jan 2017) found abuse limited to the three staff and no collusion by the state or intelligence services. Set as 'elite' for the intelligence-protection claims; the institution itself is state care.
cases.cite: Historical Institutional Abuse Inquiry report, 20 Jan 2017 (via Wikipedia 'Kincora Boys' Home')

cases.n: Lord Nazir Ahmed — convicted of offences against two children in the 1970s
cases.who: Nazir Ahmed (former Labour peer)
cases.d: On 5 Jan 2022 the former peer was convicted of attempted rape of a girl and a serious sexual assault on a boy committed in 1971–1974, when he was a teenager. He was sentenced to 5½ years (reduced to 2½ on appeal in March 2023). He had left the Lords in 2020 over a separate complaint.
cases.cite: Sheffield Crown Court, Jan–Feb 2022 (via Wikipedia 'Nazir Ahmed, Baron Ahmed')

cases.n: Imran Ahmad Khan MP — sexual assault of a 15-year-old boy
cases.who: Imran Ahmad Khan (Conservative MP for Wakefield)
cases.d: A sitting MP, Khan was convicted on 11 Apr 2022 of sexually assaulting a 15-year-old boy in 2008, expelled from the Conservative Party, resigned his seat, and was sentenced to 18 months; his appeal failed in Dec 2022.
cases.cite: Southwark Crown Court, Apr–May 2022 (via Wikipedia 'Imran Ahmad Khan')

cases.n: Sebastian Edathy (Bundestag) — images of naked minors; case closed on payment
cases.who: Sebastian Edathy (SPD member of the Bundestag)
cases.cover: Interior Minister Hans-Peter Friedrich resigned on 14 Feb 2014 after being accused of disclosing the investigation to SPD leaders.
cases.d: Edathy resigned from the Bundestag on 7 Feb 2014; his home and offices were searched on 9 Feb over material bought from a Canadian company. In March 2015 he admitted downloading images and videos of naked minors on his official laptop and the Verden court ended the trial against a €5,000 payment; he has no conviction.
cases.cite: Verden District Court, March 2015 (via Wikipedia 'Sebastian Edathy')

cases.n: Jean Succar Kuri — Cancún child sexual exploitation ring
cases.who: Jean Succar Kuri (hotelier); associates named in Lydia Cacho's reporting
cases.cover: See the related record on journalist Lydia Cacho's 2005 arrest arranged after her book exposed the ring.
cases.d: Hotel businessman Succar Kuri was detained in Chandler, Arizona in 2004 and extradited to Mexico (2006). On 31 Aug 2011 he was sentenced to 112 years for child pornography and corruption of minors; the conviction was upheld in 2016. He died in Cancún in 2024. Journalist Lydia Cacho's book 'Los demonios del Edén' linked him to Puebla businessman Kamel Nacif.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Jean Succar Kuri' (citing El Universal, CBS)

cases.n: Lydia Cacho's arrest — Puebla governor and businessman protected exploitation ring
cases.who: Mario Marín (Governor of Puebla); Kamel Nacif Borge (businessman)
cases.cover: Intimidation of a journalist: after Cacho exposed the Cancún ring, Puebla police arrested her in Cancún and drove her about 900 miles to Puebla. Leaked calls (La Jornada, 14 Feb 2006) recorded Nacif and Marín discussing jailing her as a favour and having her abused in jail. Mexico's Supreme Court ruled 6–4 on 29 Nov 2007 that Marín had no case to answer.
cases.d: A federal court issued arrest warrants in April 2019 against Marín and Nacif for the torture of Cacho. Marín was arrested in Acapulco on 3 Feb 2021. As of 2023 reporting he remained in custody; his current trial status was not confirmed. Nacif's status was not confirmed.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Lydia Cacho'; Wikipedia (es) 'Mario Marín Torres' (citing La Jornada, FGR)

cases.n: Spiniak case, Chile — child exploitation ring and false accusation against a senator
cases.victims_note: 25 adolescents named as potential victims in 2004; convictions covered five minors
cases.who: Claudio Spiniak (businessman)
cases.d: Businessman Claudio Spiniak was arrested on 30 Sept 2003 accused of running a paedophile network; in 2008 the Supreme Court sentenced him to 12 years (later 10) for abusing five minors. Witness Gema Bueno accused Senator Jovino Novoa of attending abuse parties, then admitted in Aug 2004 that she had lied; she and a priest who induced her were convicted of false testimony (upheld 2008). Novoa and other politicians named were cleared — the political-network claim is disproved.
cases.cite: Chilean Supreme Court, 7 Aug 2008 (via Wikipedia (es) 'Caso Spiniak')

cases.n: Larry Nassar — USA Gymnastics and Michigan State University
cases.victims_note: at least 265 identified; more than 500 athletes made allegations
cases.who: Larry Nassar (team doctor); USA Gymnastics; Michigan State University; FBI; US Olympic & Paralympic Committee
cases.cover: Athletes complained as early as 1997. USAG was told on 17 June 2015. The DOJ Inspector General (July 2021) found FBI agents failed to act on the gymnasts' reports and that supervisory agent W. Jay Abbott later lied about it. MSU dean William Strampel was convicted of misconduct in office (2019); charges against ex-MSU president Lou Anna Simon (dismissed 2020) and ex-USAG CEO Steve Penny (dropped 2022) did not end in convictions; coach Kathie Klages's conviction was overturned (2021). USA Gymnastics had complaints against 54 coaches 1996–2006.
cases.d: Nassar pleaded guilty to federal child-abuse-image charges (60 years, Dec 2017) and was sentenced in Michigan to 40–175 years (Jan 2018) and 40–125 years (Feb 2018). Settlements: Michigan State $500m (2018); USAG and USOPC $380m (Dec 2021); the US government $138.7m over FBI failures (2024). Abuse also occurred at the Karolyi Ranch national training centre in Texas. IndyStar's Sept 2016 investigation triggered the case.
cases.cite: DOJ OIG report on FBI handling of Nassar allegations, July 2021; Wikipedia 'Larry Nassar' and 'USA Gymnastics sex abuse scandal'

cases.n: Jerry Sandusky — Penn State football and The Second Mile
cases.who: Jerry Sandusky (assistant coach); Pennsylvania State University; The Second Mile charity
cases.cover: A 1998 report to Penn State police was not prosecuted. In 2001 graduate assistant Mike McQueary reported seeing Sandusky with a boy in a shower; it went to Joe Paterno, athletic director Tim Curley and vice-president Gary Schultz. The Freeh report (July 2012) found Paterno, president Graham Spanier, Curley and Schultz concealed Sandusky's activities. Curley, Schultz and Spanier were convicted of child endangerment in 2017.
cases.d: Sandusky was charged in Nov 2011 and convicted on 22 June 2012 of 45 of 48 counts involving 10 boys, then sentenced to 30–60 years. The NCAA fined Penn State $60m. By Nov 2015 Penn State owed close to $93m to victims. Sandusky met boys through The Second Mile charity he founded in 1977.
cases.cite: Freeh report, 12 July 2012; Centre County court, 2012 (via Wikipedia 'Penn State child sex abuse scandal')

cases.n: Dennis Hastert — former House Speaker admitted abusing boys he coached
cases.victims_note: prosecutors said at least four boys, some as young as 14
cases.who: Dennis Hastert (Speaker of the US House 1999–2007; former wrestling coach)
cases.cover: Hush money: he withdrew about $952,000 in structured cash payments to a former student; the statute of limitations meant no sex-crime charge was possible.
cases.d: Hastert was indicted in May 2015 for structuring cash withdrawals and lying to the FBI, and pleaded guilty to structuring in Oct 2015. At sentencing in April 2016 he admitted sexually abusing boys he coached at Yorkville High School (1965–1981); the judge called him a 'serial child molester' and sentenced him to 15 months. He was never convicted of a sexual offence.
cases.cite: US District Court, N.D. Illinois, April 2016 (via Wikipedia 'Dennis Hastert')

cases.n: Mark Foley — messages to congressional pages; House leadership 'negligent'
cases.who: Rep. Mark Foley; House Republican leadership
cases.cover: Complaints reached House staff and leaders around 2000–2005. The House Ethics Committee (Dec 2006) found Speaker Hastert and other leaders 'negligent' but recommended no sanctions. Florida's FDLE closed its probe in 2008 citing insufficient evidence and said Congress and Foley denied it access to data.
cases.d: In Sept 2006 sexually explicit emails and messages from Rep. Foley to teenage former House pages became public; he resigned on 29 Sept 2006. No criminal charges were brought.
cases.cite: House Committee on Standards of Official Conduct report, Dec 2006 (via Wikipedia 'Mark Foley scandal')

cases.n: Joel Greenberg conviction and House Ethics findings on Matt Gaetz
cases.who: Joel Greenberg (Seminole County tax collector); Rep. Matt Gaetz (not charged)
cases.d: Greenberg pleaded guilty on 17 May 2021 to sex trafficking of a 17-year-old girl in 2017 and other charges and was sentenced to 11 years (1 Dec 2022). DOJ investigated Rep. Gaetz over the same girl but did not charge him. The House Ethics Committee report (Dec 2024) found evidence Gaetz paid for sex, including with the 17-year-old in 2017, but insufficient evidence of sex trafficking under federal law. Gaetz denies sexual contact with a minor.
cases.cite: US District Court, M.D. Florida; House Ethics Committee report, Dec 2024 (via Wikipedia 'Joel Greenberg (politician)' and 'Matt Gaetz')

cases.n: R. Kelly — racketeering and child sexual abuse material convictions
cases.who: Robert Kelly (singer) and his entourage (racketeering enterprise)
cases.cover: He was acquitted in 2008 of child pornography charges brought in 2002, despite Chicago Sun-Times reporting from 2000.
cases.d: A Brooklyn federal jury convicted Kelly on 27 Sept 2021 of racketeering and Mann Act sex-trafficking offences, including against minors (30 years). In 2022 a Chicago federal jury convicted him of producing child sexual abuse material and enticing minors, adding a further sentence in 2023. The 2019 documentary 'Surviving R. Kelly' led to the new prosecutions.
cases.cite: EDNY and NDIL verdicts 2021–2022 (via Wikipedia 'R. Kelly')

cases.n: NXIVM — Keith Raniere racketeering incl. sexual exploitation of a child
cases.victims_note: predicate acts included the sexual exploitation of a 15-year-old girl
cases.who: NXIVM; Keith Raniere; Clare Bronfman (heiress, convicted of immigration and ID offences)
cases.d: On 19 June 2019 a Brooklyn jury convicted Raniere of racketeering; predicate acts included sexual exploitation of a child and possession of abuse material involving a 15-year-old. He was sentenced to 120 years on 27 Oct 2020. Funder Clare Bronfman received 81 months for related immigration and identity offences.
cases.cite: EDNY verdict 19 June 2019 (via Wikipedia 'NXIVM')

cases.n: Jared Fogle (Subway spokesman) — child abuse material and paid sex with minors
cases.who: Jared Fogle; Russell Taylor (co-conspirator); Subway
cases.cover: Allegations surfaced in 2007 but the FBI acted only in 2015. A franchisee says she told Subway in 2008 about Fogle's messages seeking sex with a minor; Subway says it has no record.
cases.d: Arrested on 7 July 2015, Fogle pleaded guilty to distributing and receiving child abuse material and travelling to engage in illicit sexual conduct with a minor, and was sentenced to 15 years 8 months on 19 Nov 2015, with $1.4m restitution to 14 victims.
cases.cite: US District Court, S.D. Indiana, Nov 2015 (via Wikipedia 'Jared Fogle')

cases.n: Brian Peck — Nickelodeon dialogue coach convicted of abusing a child actor
cases.who: Brian Peck (Nickelodeon dialogue coach)
cases.cover: Several entertainment-industry figures wrote letters supporting Peck at sentencing in 2004; some apologised in 2024.
cases.d: Peck was arrested on 19 Aug 2003 and pleaded no contest in May 2004 to a lewd act on a 14–15-year-old and oral copulation with a minor; he was sentenced to 16 months. The victim, actor Drake Bell, identified himself publicly in the March 2024 documentary 'Quiet on Set'.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Brian Peck' (citing LA court records, Investigation Discovery)

cases.n: Roman Polanski — 1977 guilty plea, fugitive since 1978
cases.who: Roman Polanski (film director)
cases.cover: Fled to France on 1 Feb 1978 before sentencing; Switzerland (2010) and Poland (2015–16) refused US extradition.
cases.d: Arrested on 10 March 1977 for offences against a 13-year-old girl, Polanski pleaded guilty to unlawful sexual intercourse with a minor. He fled before sentencing and has lived mainly in France. Swiss police detained him in 2009 but Switzerland refused extradition in July 2010; Poland's Supreme Court refused in Dec 2016. A 2023 civil suit alleging rape of a minor in 1973 was settled in 2024.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Roman Polanski sexual abuse case'

cases.n: Michael Jackson — 1993 allegations settled, 2005 acquittal
cases.who: Michael Jackson (singer)
cases.d: A 1993 allegation by a 13-year-old led two grand juries to decline to indict; Jackson settled the family's civil suit in Jan 1994 for a reported $23m without admission. He was charged in Dec 2003 with molesting a 13-year-old and acquitted on all 10 counts on 13 June 2005. No criminal finding exists against him.
cases.cite: Santa Barbara County Superior Court verdict, 13 June 2005 (via Wikipedia 'Trial of Michael Jackson')

cases.n: Graham James — junior hockey coach (Western Hockey League)
cases.victims_note: convictions for at least four players across 1997 and 2012 cases
cases.who: Graham James (coach/GM, Swift Current Broncos, Calgary Hitmen)
cases.cover: He received a federal pardon in 2007, which became public in 2010.
cases.d: James pleaded guilty in Jan 1997 to sexually assaulting two players, including Sheldon Kennedy (3½ years). After Theo Fleury's 2009 memoir and complaint he pleaded guilty in Dec 2011 to assaults on Fleury and Todd Holt; the 2-year sentence was raised to 5 years on appeal in Feb 2013.
cases.cite: Manitoba Court of Appeal, 15 Feb 2013 (via Wikipedia 'Graham James (ice hockey)')

cases.n: USA Swimming — coaches banned for abuse; claims mishandled
cases.victims_note: 'hundreds' of swimmers' claims allegedly mishandled (Orange County Register, 2018)
cases.who: USA Swimming
cases.d: USA Swimming banned coach Rick Curl for life in 2012 and former Olympic coach Mitch Ivey in 2013. A 2018 Orange County Register investigation reported hundreds of swimmers whose abuse claims were allegedly mishandled or ignored. Former coach Andy King is serving 40 years after pleading no contest to 20 child molestation charges.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'USA Swimming' (citing Orange County Register, 2018)

cases.n: Franklin credit union 'child prostitution ring' allegations, Nebraska
cases.who: Claims against Lawrence E. King Jr. (Franklin Community Federal Credit Union) and prominent Nebraskans
cases.d: After federal agents raided the Franklin credit union in Nov 1988 over a $38m embezzlement, claims spread that its manager Lawrence King hosted parties where minors were abused. In July 1990 a Douglas County grand jury called the claims a 'carefully crafted hoax' and indicted two accusers for perjury; a federal grand jury in Sept 1990 also found them unfounded. King pleaded guilty to embezzlement (15 years). A 1999 $1m civil default judgment against King, who did not respond, is not a finding of fact.
cases.cite: Douglas County grand jury report, July 1990 (via Wikipedia 'Franklin child prostitution ring allegations')

cases.n: 'Pizzagate' — false claim of a child-trafficking ring at a Washington pizzeria
cases.who: Online conspiracy theory targeting Democratic politicians
cases.d: In Oct–Nov 2016 online posts claimed Democrats ran a child-abuse ring from Comet Ping Pong, citing leaked Podesta emails. DC police called it 'fictitious'; the restaurant has no basement and no victims or evidence emerged. On 4 Dec 2016 Edgar Maddison Welch fired a rifle inside; he pleaded guilty and was jailed for four years (June 2017).
cases.cite: US District Court for DC, 22 June 2017 (via Wikipedia 'Pizzagate conspiracy theory')

cases.n: McMartin preschool trial — 'satanic abuse' panic ends in acquittals
cases.who: McMartin Preschool (accused: Ray Buckey, Peggy McMartin Buckey)
cases.d: After a 1983 accusation, investigators claimed 360 children had been abused, using interview techniques later judged coercive. Peggy McMartin Buckey was acquitted on all counts in Jan 1990; Ray Buckey was acquitted on 52 counts and two juries deadlocked on the rest, so charges were dropped. There were no convictions after seven years and about $15m. Included as the template for 'ritual abuse' claims; not an elite case strictly.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'McMartin preschool trial'

cases.n: Johnny Kitagawa — Johnny & Associates talent agency
cases.victims_note: Smile-Up (successor company) had received 1,044 claims by 14 Aug 2026 and decided to compensate 585
cases.who: Johnny Kitagawa (founder, Johnny & Associates; now Smile-Up)
cases.cover: Media silence: Shukan Bunshun's 2001 reports were upheld on the sexual allegations by the courts (damages reduced 2003; Supreme Court rejected appeal 2004), yet Japanese media barely covered them; journalists attributed this to the agency's power over talent bookings. Earliest cited report: Weekly Sankei, 1965.
cases.d: An independent investigation reported on 29 Aug 2023 that Kitagawa repeatedly sexually abused boys and young men from the early 1970s to the mid-2010s. The company admitted the abuse on 7 Sept 2023, renamed itself Smile-Up and began compensation in Nov 2023. The BBC documentary 'Predator' (March 2023) and Kauan Okamoto's April 2023 testimony triggered the reckoning. Kitagawa died in 2019 and was never charged.
cases.cite: Johnny & Associates external special investigation team report, 29 Aug 2023 (via Wikipedia 'Johnny Kitagawa' and 'Johnny & Associates')

cases.n: Unnao rape case — MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar
cases.who: Kuldeep Singh Sengar (BJP MLA, Uttar Pradesh)
cases.cover: The victim's father died in police custody; in July 2019 a truck crash killed two of her aunts and critically injured her and her lawyer (a court later accepted the CBI finding of no foul play in the crash). The arrest came only after the Allahabad High Court ordered it in 2018.
cases.d: Sengar raped a 16-year-old girl in June 2017 who came to him seeking a job. He was convicted in Dec 2019 by a Delhi court of kidnapping and raping a minor. On 23 Dec 2025 the Delhi High Court suspended his sentence; the Supreme Court stayed that order on 29 Dec 2025 while it hears the case.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Kuldeep Singh Sengar' (citing Indian Express, The Hindu)

cases.n: Kasur child abuse video scandal (Hussain Khanwala)
cases.victims_note: Pakistani media estimate 280–300 children, mostly boys; up to 400 videos
cases.who: Local gang filming abuse of children; Punjab police; local MPA (alleged)
cases.cover: Punjab police and the local PML-N provincial assembly member Malik Ahmad Saeed Khan were alleged to have tried to cover it up; the Punjab law minister called the reports a land dispute. Police clashed with protesting villagers on 8 Aug 2015.
cases.d: In August 2015 The Nation reported that a gang in Hussain Khanwala had filmed the abuse of about 280 children between 2006 and 2014 and used the videos to blackmail families. Placed in 'elite' for the alleged political protection; convictions were not verified for this record.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Kasur child sexual abuse scandal' (citing The Nation, Aug 2015)

cases.n: Apollo Quiboloy — US sex-trafficking indictment and Philippine child-abuse charges
cases.who: Apollo Quiboloy; Kingdom of Jesus Christ church (KOJC)
cases.cover: Close ally and spiritual adviser of President Rodrigo Duterte, who lent him aircraft; he evaded Philippine arrest warrants for months in 2024 and refused a Senate summons.
cases.d: A US grand jury indicted Quiboloy in Nov 2021 for conspiracy to conduct sex trafficking, including of minors, and other crimes; the US sanctioned him in Dec 2022. In March–April 2024 Philippine prosecutors filed qualified trafficking and child-abuse charges. He was taken into custody in Davao on 8 Sept 2024 after a siege of the KOJC compound. No verdict as of the latest source; extradition status unconfirmed. Religious leader placed under 'elite' for political protection.
cases.cite: US District Court, C.D. California indictment, Nov 2021; Wikipedia 'Apollo Quiboloy'

cases.n: Bacha bazi — boys abused by Afghan commanders; US forces told not to intervene
cases.who: Afghan police and militia commanders; US military
cases.cover: NYT (Sept 2015) reported US soldiers were told to ignore abuse by Afghan allies; a Nov 2017 DoD Inspector General report found some troops were told 'nothing could be done'. A June 2017 SIGAR report noted 75 reports of gross human-rights violations under review, 7 involving child sexual assault; aid cutoffs required by US law never happened.
cases.d: Bacha bazi is the sexual exploitation of boys kept as 'dancers' by powerful men. Cases include an Afghan Local Police commander who chained and raped a 12-year-old boy in Kunduz (2011). Afghanistan criminalised the practice in its Feb 2018 penal code. A 2014 AIHRC study found it 'normal and customary' in some areas. Overlaps with the 'conflict' setting.
cases.cite: SIGAR report, June 2017; DoD Inspector General DODIG-2018-018, Nov 2017 (via Wikipedia 'Bacha bazi')

cases.n: Knox Grammar School — headmaster failed to report teachers' abuse
cases.who: Knox Grammar School; Uniting Church
cases.cover: The Royal Commission (Sept 2016) found headmaster Ian Paterson never reported a student's abuse allegation to police in about 30 years, despite a duty from 1988; he let accused teachers resign and gave some positive references, and withheld information from a police officer.
cases.d: In 2009 five former teachers were charged with sex offences from 1976–1990 and all were convicted. The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse held case study 23 in 2015 and reported in Sept 2016.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Case Study 23 report, Sept 2016 (via Wikipedia 'Knox Grammar School')

cases.n: Geelong Grammar School — Royal Commission case study 32
cases.who: Geelong Grammar School (Anglican)
cases.cover: The Royal Commission found the school repeatedly failed to investigate or report credible allegations, particularly under principal John Lewis (1980–94), and 'placed its own interests ahead of those of victims'. A 2007 settlement with victims of a boarding-house assistant was minuted as 'a very satisfactory financial outcome for the school'.
cases.d: Former students described abuse by staff between 1956 and 1989 across four campuses. Five former staff were convicted of child sex offences, including a boarding-house assistant who pleaded guilty in 2005 to 41 offences against 40 boys.
cases.cite: Royal Commission Case Study 32 report, 2016–17 (via Wikipedia 'Geelong Grammar School')

cases.n: Brisbane Grammar / St Paul's — counsellor abuse; Governor-General resigns over church handling
cases.victims_note: about 70 former Brisbane Grammar students sued over counsellor Kevin Lynch
cases.who: Brisbane Grammar School; St Paul's School; Anglican Diocese of Brisbane (Archbishop Peter Hollingworth)
cases.cover: Brisbane Grammar quietly investigated complaints about counsellor Kevin Lynch in the early 1980s; he moved to St Paul's. A 2003 diocesan inquiry found Archbishop Hollingworth in 1993 allowed a known abuser to keep working as a priest.
cases.d: Lynch, counsellor at Brisbane Grammar 1976–1988, was charged in Jan 1997 and died by suicide the next day. Hollingworth, then Governor-General of Australia, resigned on 26 May 2003 after the diocesan report was tabled in the Queensland parliament. The Royal Commission held case study 34 on these schools in 2015.
cases.cite: Anglican Diocese of Brisbane inquiry report, tabled May 2003; Royal Commission Case Study 34 (via Wikipedia 'Brisbane Grammar School', 'Peter Hollingworth')

cases.n: Timothy Omotoso (Jesus Dominion International) — trafficking and rape charges ended in acquittal
cases.who: Timothy Omotoso (Nigerian televangelist) and two co-accused
cases.cover: Whistleblower Pamela Mabini was shot dead outside her home on 7 March 2025, weeks before the verdict.
cases.d: Omotoso was arrested on 20 April 2017 and charged with rape, human trafficking and racketeering, with prosecutors alleging he abused young women, some as young as 14. On 2 April 2025 the Eastern Cape High Court acquitted him and two co-accused, finding the prosecution had failed to prove guilt, citing prosecutorial mishandling. He was arrested on immigration grounds in May 2025.
cases.cite: Eastern Cape High Court, 2 April 2025 (via Wikipedia 'Timothy Omotoso')

cases.n: T.B. Joshua (SCOAN) — BBC investigation into abuse of disciples
cases.who: T.B. Joshua; Synagogue Church of All Nations (SCOAN)
cases.d: A two-year BBC investigation published in January 2024 reported that more than 25 former followers alleged abuse by Joshua and the church over 15+ years, including rapes and forced abortions. One woman said he first raped her at 17. Joshua died in June 2021; the church denies the allegations. No official finding. Religious figure placed here for celebrity and political influence.
cases.cite: BBC News investigation, Jan 2024 (via Wikipedia 'T. B. Joshua')

cases.n: Bob Hewitt — tennis coach convicted of raping girls he coached
cases.victims_note: victims aged 12–14
cases.who: Bob Hewitt (Grand Slam doubles champion, coach)
cases.d: On 23 March 2015 the South Gauteng High Court convicted former tennis champion Bob Hewitt of two rapes and one sexual assault of girls he coached in 1975–1982; he got an effective six years (appeal rejected 2016). The International Tennis Hall of Fame expelled him in 2016.
cases.cite: South Gauteng High Court, 23 Mar 2015 (via Wikipedia 'Bob Hewitt')

cases.n: Haitian Football Federation — Yves Jean-Bart banned by FIFA
cases.who: Yves Jean-Bart (FHF president since 2000)
cases.d: On 30 April 2020 Jean-Bart was accused of sexually abusing young female players at the federation's training centre; on 20 Nov 2020 FIFA's Ethics Committee banned him for life. Reports that the Court of Arbitration for Sport later annulled the ban (2023) could not be confirmed from an opened source in this pass, so status is set to 'alleged' pending check.
cases.cite: FIFA Ethics Committee decision, 20 Nov 2020 (via Wikipedia 'Yves Jean-Bart')

cases.n: Whyte Review — British Gymnastics
cases.who: British Gymnastics
cases.d: Anne Whyte KC's review, published June 2022, received more than 400 submissions describing sexual assault alongside emotional abuse and excessive weight control. Most of its findings concern non-sexual abuse; the sexual-abuse case count was not stated in the source opened.
cases.cite: The Whyte Review, June 2022 (via Wikipedia 'Whyte Review')

cases.n: Wrestling Federation of India — Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh (minor's complaint closed)
cases.who: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh (BJP MP, WFI president)
cases.d: After Olympic wrestlers protested from January 2023, Delhi Police registered two FIRs on 28 April 2023, following Supreme Court intervention: one under the child-protection POCSO Act for a minor, one for six adult wrestlers. On 27 May 2025 a Delhi court cleared him in the minor's case. Charges were framed in the adult wrestlers' case, which continues (adults are outside this map's scope).
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh' (citing Indian Express, The Hindu)

cases.n: Bibbiano ('Angeli e Demoni') — investigation into unlawful removal of children
cases.who: Val d'Enza social services; mayor Andrea Carletti (house arrest 2019)
cases.d: In June 2019 Italian police said they had uncovered a group accused of manipulating children's testimony to remove them from families and place them with foster parents; Bibbiano's mayor Andrea Carletti was placed under house arrest (confirmed Aug 2019). The trial outcomes for the defendants were NOT verified in this pass and must be checked before publication; this belongs more naturally in the 'adoption' setting.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Bibbiano' (citing ANSA/press, June–Aug 2019)

nets.reach_note: Documented by courts: New York, Palm Beach, New Mexico, London (Maxwell trial), US Virgin Islands (USVI suits), Paris (French criminal probe). Turkey and Czech Republic appear only in a 2009 civil complaint stated 'upon information and belief'. Norway and Israel are listed for documented political/financial ties (Jagland charge; Barak business ties), not abuse findings.
nets.d: Financier Jeffrey Epstein (d. 2019) and Ghislaine Maxwell (convicted 2021) sexually abused and trafficked girls, some as young as 14, between at least 1994 and 2005 across homes in New York, Palm Beach, New Mexico, the US Virgin Islands, Paris and London. Model agent Jean-Luc Brunel was charged in France and died in custody. Banks paid hundreds of millions in settlements. 2025–2026 file releases led to misconduct and corruption inquiries against officials in the UK and Norway.
nets.cite: Court records via AP/PBS; DOJ OIG 2023; Wikipedia 'Jeffrey Epstein'

nets.n: Jimmy Savile and the institutions that hosted him (BBC, NHS)
nets.d: Savile used his BBC celebrity and NHS fundraising roles to gain access to children and patients for decades. Inquiries found 72 victims linked to the BBC (Smith, 2016) and victims aged 5–75 across NHS sites (Lampard, 2015); the Met recorded 214 crimes (2013).
nets.cite: Smith Review 2016; Lampard 2015; Giving Victims a Voice 2013

nets.d: Metropolitan Police investigation opened 19 Oct 2012 after the Savile revelations; 19 arrests and 7 convictions of entertainment figures.

Japan's dominant boy-band talent agency. Its founder Johnny Kitagawa abused boys and young men from the early 1970s to the mid-2010s (independent investigation, 2023); the company admitted it and by Aug 2026 had decided to compensate 585 people.

flows.n: Kevin Lynch: Brisbane Grammar → St Paul's
flows.d: After complaints were quietly investigated at Brisbane Grammar in the early 1980s, counsellor Kevin Lynch later worked at St Paul's School, where he also abused students; he was charged in 1997.

EPSTEIN — PROVEN vs ALLEGED (as of 27 Oct 2026):
Proven by courts: Epstein's 2008 Florida conviction for soliciting a minor; Maxwell's 2021 conviction for sex trafficking of a minor (upheld; Supreme Court declined review 6 Oct 2025); abuse at homes in New York, Palm Beach, New Mexico, London; DOJ OIG found prison staff failures in his 2019 death (suicide). Official findings: OPR (2020) 'poor judgment' by Acosta; Judge Marra (2019) CVRA violation; NM truth commission interim report (Aug 2026) found likely preferential treatment by NM law enforcement and estimated 30+ people abused in NM. Civil: USVI $105m from estate; JPMorgan $290m (victims) + $75m (USVI). Political: UK police arrested Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor (19 Feb 2026) and Peter Mandelson (23 Feb 2026) on suspicion of misconduct in public office for allegedly passing government information to Epstein — neither charged with a sexual offence; Norway charged Thorbjørn Jagland with aggravated corruption (12 Feb 2026).
Not proven: a 'client list'; blackmail of clients; that Epstein 'lent out' girls to powerful men (FBI notes said other victims did not corroborate); murder; intelligence-agency employment. The 'belonged to intelligence' quote attributed to Acosta (Vicky Ward/Daily Beast, July 2019, anonymous source) was denied by Acosta, and DOJ OPR (Nov 2020) found no evidence Epstein was an intelligence asset or cooperating witness. Ari Ben-Menashe's claims concern Robert Maxwell; Congress's Iran-Contra investigators called his testimony 'not credible'. Documented but not evidence of agency work: Epstein's business ties with ex-Israeli PM Ehud Barak (Reporty/Carbyne investment, ~30 visits 2013–17). Turkey's inquiry rests on a 2009 civil complaint made 'upon information and belief'. Ongoing (Oct 2026): DOJ OIG review of Transparency Act compliance; NM AG criminal probe; UK misconduct investigations; House Democrats calling for a special counsel; Maxwell's pardon bid.
